sources.title: Baidu Java backend interview note exact permutations prompt
Permutation backtracking versus independent lexicographic next-permutation oracle

claims.text: The recoverable source asks only to hand-write a full-permutation algorithm; it does not preserve language, input representation, duplicate-value semantics, output ordering, empty-input behavior, or null behavior.

The candidate explicitly narrows its executable contract to distinct integer values, one empty permutation for an empty array, and rejection of null, while treating duplicate-value uniqueness as a separately clarified variant.

For fixed distinct inputs of sizes 0 through 8 and 120 deterministic randomized distinct arrays, the backtracking implementation has n! unique results and its result set exactly matches an independent lexicographic next-permutation enumerator.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed-n=0..8 randomized=120 oracle=lexicographic-next-permutation distinct-input=true count-factorial=true no-duplicates=true empty-one=true null-rejected=true
